Francis Cornwell
fran'sis korn'wel
n. (Francis Cornwell, c. 1590–1665, Kentish minister and Baptist controversialist)
Latin Franciscus, a Frank, a free man; English Cornwell, from a place-name meaning corn spring.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Francis Cornwell was vicar of Marden in Kent, imprisoned for refusing the ceremonies, and while in prison he came to the conviction that infant baptism had no warrant in Scripture. He was rebaptized, left the parish church, and became the leading Baptist voice in Kent, publishing on the sufficiency of Scripture against the authority of tradition and persuading others, Christopher Blackwood among them, who had come to a public disputation intending to refute him. The dictionary notes the route by which he arrived. He did not start from a theory of the church; he started from a conviction about Scripture and followed it where it went, which is the way most of the English Baptists came to their position (Isa 8:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines warrant as authority, that which authorizes an act, and tradition as the delivery of opinions or practices from father to son.

expand to see more

WAR'RANT, n. That which authorizes or justifies an act; authority; commission.

TRADI'TION, n. The delivery of opinions, doctrines, practices, rites and customs from father to son, by oral communication.

DISPUTA'TION, n. A reasoning or argumentation in opposition to something, or on opposite sides.

CONVIC'TION, n. The act of convincing, or compelling one to admit the truth of a charge or of a proposition.

Key Scripture

Isa 8:20 — "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them."

Act 17:11 — "These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so."

Mat 15:9 — "But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men."

Act 2:38 — "Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost."

Modern Corruption

A Kentish vicar who read himself out of infant baptism in prison.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The live misuse is the assumption that a change of practice must spring from a change of party. Cornwell had no Baptist congregation to join when the conviction came and no advantage in holding it; he was already in prison for a different nonconformity. He went to the texts, found no command or example of an infant baptized, and acted.

The principle to recover is that the practice of the church is tried by the written word, and that worship resting on tradition alone is vain however ancient. “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them” (Isa 8:20). Our Lord quotes Isaiah against exactly this: “in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men” (Mat 15:9). And the Bereans are commended for doing what Cornwell did: “searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so” (Act 17:11).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew teudah (H8584), testimony, attestation; Greek entalma (G1778), a precept, an injunction of men.

Hebrew torah (H8451) — law, instruction, direction; Isaiah 8:20.

Hebrew teudah (H8584) — testimony, attestation, witness; Isaiah 8:20.

Greek anakrino (G350) — to examine, to search into, to sift; Acts 17:11.

Greek entalma (G1778) — a precept, an injunction, a commandment of men; Matthew 15:9.

Greek baptizo (G907) — to dip, to immerse, to baptize; Acts 2:38.

Usage

"“To the law and to the testimony” (Isa 8:20) — a conviction reached in prison."

"“teaching for doctrines the commandments of men” (Mat 15:9) — tradition tried by the word."

"“searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so” (Act 17:11) — and Blackwood came to refute him."
